tested_scope: One local deterministic synthetic claim-adapter replay only. Initial canonical state contained exactly one committed claim for effect_identity=E with claim_identity=C1 and attempt_identity=A1. One schema-valid retry was presented with the same effect_identity=E and claim_identity=C1 but a different attempt_identity=A2. The fixture validated all required string fields, keyed canonical admission by effect_identity, and treated attempt_identity as retry-attempt metadata rather than a new effect identity. No public-source probe, repository race, production implementation, O/downstream state, other-worker state, external coordination, richer-mode execution, hosted compute, scheduler mutation, or optional second leaf was executed.
observations: Before retry, canonical claim count for effect E was exactly 1 and the stored canonical record was {effect_identity:E, claim_identity:C1, attempt_identity:A1, status:committed}.
The retry {effect_identity:E, claim_identity:C1, attempt_identity:A2} passed schema validation, then found the existing canonical record for E before any fresh-claim admission.
The fixture classified the retry as IDEMPOTENT_REPLAY and returned the existing canonical claim C1; fresh_claim_emitted=false and canonical claim count remained exactly 1.
The stored canonical record remained byte-for-byte unchanged in the modeled fields, including attempt_identity=A1, so the retry caused no partial canonical overwrite.
inference: Within this exact synthetic fixture, effect-identity-first lookup plus no-write replay handling is sufficient to suppress a duplicate effect when a valid retry arrives under a different attempt identity, while preserving the original canonical record. This does not establish simultaneous-writer, repository-CAS, external transport, fairness, or production behavior and is not Phase-1 acceptance evidence by itself.
unresolved_children: Repository-level simultaneous-writer behavior remains untested: two claimers starting from the same prior generation must not both produce a canonical effect.
Stale-CAS handling remains untested: a loser after another writer commits must fail closed without same-run spin, duplicate effect emission, or partial overwrite.
Rate-limit interruption, fairness/lease behavior, and quota-zero transport behavior remain outside this fixture's tested scope.
